ReZero: Enhancing LLM search ability by trying
one-more-time
Alan Dao (Gia Tuan Dao)1, Thinh Le1
Menlo Research
alan@menlo.ai, thinh@menlo.ai
1Equal contribution.
April 16, 2025
arXiv:2504.11001v1  [cs.CL]  15 Apr 2025
Abstract
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) improves Large
Language Model (LLM) performance on knowledgeintensive tasks but depends heavily on initial search
query quality. Current methods, often using Reinforcement Learning (RL), typically focus on query formulation
or reasoning over results, without explicitly encouraging
persistence after a failed search.
We introduce ReZero
(Retry-Zero), a novel RL framework that directly rewards
the act of retrying a search query following an initial
unsuccessful attempt. This incentivizes the LLM to explore alternative queries rather than prematurely halting.
ReZero demonstrates significant improvement, achieving
46.88% accuracy compared to a 25% baseline. By rewarding persistence, ReZero enhances LLM robustness in complex information-seeking scenarios where initial queries
may prove insufficient.
